messages:
samir: quick follow-up on the "attenuation adapter" prototype i pushed. Purpose: attenuate short noisy bursts (probing/scraping) before they hit central quota engines. want feedback on the admission API and failure modes.

maria: sketch the typical request flow please? is adapter in-path at the edge or as a filter before the rate service?

samir: adapter lives at the edge proxy as a lightweight filter. flow: ingress -> adapter -> rate-limiter -> origin. adapter returns hints to the proxy to shape immediate retry/backoff behavior and an optional fingerprint for the rate-limiter to use.

aaron: two interface patterns: 1) advisory hints (non-binding) where rate-limiter stays authoritative, 2) binding pre-admit where adapter can short-circuit and reject. advisory keeps boundaries cleaner and easier to roll back.

jyoti: performance is the blocker. adapter must be <2ms p50 on the hot path. any per-request cross-node lookups kill us. prefer per-node micro-shards + occasional async feed to central store for heavy hitters.

samir: prototype uses a tiny per-node sliding window + async heavy-hitter replication via a compact delta stream. it emits an "attenuation_hint" proto to the proxy. sample hint below.

samir: ```yaml
attenuation_hint:
  score: 0.0..1.0
  backoff_ms: [50, 200, 800]
  escalate: none|soft|hard
  fingerprint: "sha256:..."  # optional, node-local ttl
  reversible: true
  reason: replay|pattern|short-seq
  ttl_s: 300
```

aaron: add a field for confidence and a suggested metric tag so we can aggregate by reason. also mark whether fingerprint is server-signed to avoid client poisoning.

maria: on identity: algorithmic fingerprints are helpful but attack surface increases if adversaries attempt churn. require either API-key or signed client-id to tie fingerprints. fallback to IP only for anonymous endpoints.

jyoti: telemetry: record hint.score histogram, hint.backoff distribution, fraction of requests with escalate != none, and false-positive probes. add synthetic gate tests too.

samir: tradeoffs we debated: stateful counters give better detection but memory/ops cost. stateless probabilistic heuristics (e.g., HT bloom + rate) are cheap but higher FP. compromise: small LRU + bloom for cross-node heavy hitters.

aaron: also consider attack that rotates many client-ids to evade per-id windows. we should add cluster-level anomaly detection that watches fingerprint cardinality and entropy. if entropy spikes, automatically shift to conservative global shedding mode.

maria: policy surface: we need a config for per-route attenuation thresholds, and an operator-visible switch to force-allow/force-deny. and RBAC for who can toggle.

jyoti: rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 at 1% traffic for 24h -> 5% for 24h -> 25% -> 100. include automatic rollback on latency or error-rate regressions.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: 2025-03-04T10:00:00Z region=us-west-2 pct=1

samir: testing matrix: unit tests of hint parsing, perf harness under realistic p95+load, replay-sim tests to measure TP/FP, and chaos tests where rate-limiter drops. success criterion: <0.5% FP baseline, p50 add <1ms, p95 add <5ms.

aaron: implementation note: make hint schema extensible versioned (v1). adapter should emit a minimal JSON blob so proxies / rate-limiter don't need deep coupling.

maria: privacy note: fingerprints are server-derived and TTL-limited; store only hashes, rotate signing key quarterly, log retention 7d by default. document KMS usage for signing keys.

jyoti: infra ops: add feature-flag + per-region kill-switch, dashboard with attenuation_p95_by_region, fingerprint-churn_rate, and heavy-hitter replication lag. create alert when attenuation_p95 increases 3x over baseline.

samir: action items: @maria update schema with confidence & metric tag (EOD). @aaron propose memory budget for per-node LRU + heavy-hitter replication design (tomorrow). @jyoti prod dashboard and rollback playbook. i'll open RFC follow-up PR with sample adapter code and canary manifest.

maria: fine by me. quick Q: do we want adapter hints logged to trace spans? helpful for debugging but could be noisy.

aaron: include trace-level conditional logging and a sampling policy (0.1% default, 100% for errors).

jyoti: will add sampling and a trace tag. also ensure synthetic attacker test injects churn and measures fingerprint collision rate.

samir: thanks team. unless any veto i'll schedule the canary for the date above. :thumbsup:

aaron: +1

maria: +1 on canary, watching privacy section

jyoti: prepping monitors

samir: (pushing PR link) https://git.internal/repo/rfcs/attenuation-adapter/followup

deploy-bot: canary deployed: us-west-2 pct=1 status=ok (2025-03-04T10:05:12Z)
